title: No priests to Saints—yet confraternities and sodalities uniquely adore and invoke them, especially Mary
source_text: XXV. Quamvis autem non liceat, secundum Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae, instituere Sanctis Sacerdotes, attamen quod proxime accedit, usitatum est in illa Ecclesia in honorem Sanctorum, ac praesertim Mariae Virginis instituere confraternitates atque sodalitia, quae se eorum cultui ac venerationi peculiariter dicant, ac pro instituto suo, singulari quadam ratione illos adorant & invocant.
pass_a_gloss: Although however it is not lawful, according to the Doctors of the Roman Church, to institute Priests to the Saints, yet what comes nearest, it is customary in that Church to institute in honor of the Saints, and especially of Mary the Virgin, confraternities and sodalities, which peculiarly dedicate themselves to their cult and veneration, and by their institute, in a certain singular way, adore and invoke them.
pass_b_english: Rome bars priests of Saints, yet proliferates confraternities and sodalities.
Those societies specially adore and invoke their patrons—Mary foremost.

choices.why: The forbidden parallel office Rome still approximates by sodalities.
